描述_EN: the artisans had to first make outer moulds composed of several sections around a prototype of the finished bronze and then reproduce the patterns in reverse on the surface of the sections. the cost, craftsmanship and labor required to produce these items further emphasises their value. they would then assemble the moulds around a core leaving a space between the outer and inner parts into which melted bronze would be poured. it was probably used as a communal drinking goblet or libation cup during the traditional rites for the ancestors celebrated by members of the royal family. it was made at the end of the shang dynasty, about 1150-1050 bc, probably in the capital anyang. bronze vessels like this were kept in temples for ceremonies or buried in graves to denote status and prestige. once the bronze had solidified, the outer moulds and the inner core were removed. the ownership and use of this and other ritual vessels were essential components of the ruling system under the shang kings, and contributed to their power and authority. this vessel, called a gu in chinese, is an exquisite example of bronze craftsmanship.
描述_ZN: 工匠们必须首先在成品青铜器的原型周围制作由几个部分组成的外模，然后在这些部分的表面反向复制图案。 生产这些物品所需的成本、工艺和劳动力进一步强调了其价值。 他们会把模具组装在一个核心部分周围，在外部和内部之间留出一个空间，把融化的青铜倒进去。 它可能是在皇室成员庆祝祖先的传统仪式上作为公共饮酒的高脚杯或奠酒杯。 它是在商朝末期，大约公元前1150-1050年制造的，可能是在首都安阳。 像这样的青铜器被保存在寺庙里进行仪式，或埋在坟墓里以表示地位和声望。 一旦青铜凝固，外部模具和内部核心就会被移除。 这个和其他礼器的拥有和使用是商王统治体系的重要组成部分，有助于他们的权力和权威。 这个容器在中国被称为古，是青铜工艺的一个精致的例子。
